subject: Cross-border servicing constraints & hosting pathway qualification
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicfin.se>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00+02:00
Subject: Cross-border servicing constraints & hosting pathway qualification

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the open questions we promised to capture after our discovery: 

Call summary (brief):
- Primary objective: embed transaction enrichment and anonymized chat summarization into Nordic FinServ's customer support workflow.
- Traffic profile: peak 120 qps for short requests (~150 tokens avg).
- Data residency requirement: customer data (PII + transaction metadata) must remain in the EU for core flows; a small set of aggregated telemetry may be permitted to traverse to APAC for analytics, pending legal.

Key qualification items we need to confirm to pick a serving mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):
1) Cross-border processing: is ANY customer PII allowed to leave EU-controlled infrastructure (even to Redwood-managed APAC infra) under current policy?
2) If not, will a Dedicated or Private deployment be acceptable for APAC-located workloads, or do you prefer one central EU-only model?
3) Compliance needs: SOC 2 + local audit logging requirements and KMS controls (customer-managed KMS expected?).
4) Timeline: procurement window (SOW/PO) target: Nov 2026? Any accelerated pilots?

Next steps I'm proposing:
- I will send a short residency checklist (attached) capturing the above items and an initial recommended mapping of flows to deployment modes.
- If EU-only is mandatory for PII, we recommend starting with Hosted API in our EU region for R&D + canary traffic, then evaluate Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for production cross-account isolation.
- We'll loop in our security lead (Marissa) to confirm logging/KMS approach and provide sample configs.

Attachments: residency-checklist.xlsx (one-page table), redwood-network-diagram.png.

Can you confirm the PII residency constraint and the tentative procurement timeline?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: residency-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB), redwood-network-diagram.png (png, 120KB)

From: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicfin.se>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@nordicfin.se>
Date: 2026-09-07T11:03:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border servicing constraints & hosting pathway qualification

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Short answer on PII: EU residency required for any dataset that can be tied back to an identifiable customer (transaction ids, full names, national IDs). Aggregated telemetry (no identifiers) may be processed outside EU for analytics but must be explicitly anonymized.
- KMS: we require customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for any environment holding PII; please indicate if that is available for Dedicated and Private VPC options.
- Timeline: procurement aims to sign a pilot SOW by end of Q4 2026; production rollout targeted H1 2027. We may accelerate a POC if the data path strictly stays within EU and we can get a security assessment by mid-Oct.

Legal Ops: attaching a short checklist of questions — please review and confirm whether Redwood can provide the requested artifacts (SOC 2 reports, retention policy, audit logs).

Best,
Anna
Head of Cloud Platforms 
Nordic FinServ AB

---
Attachment stubs: legal-questions.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-08T08:21:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border servicing constraints & hosting pathway qualification

Aditya — quick internal note before I pick up with Anna: 

- KMS: we can support customer-managed KMS in Private VPC and Dedicated deployments; Hosted API (multi-tenant) supports envelope encryption but not CMK import for EU-hosted customers today.
- Routing: EU-only routing is possible for both Hosted (EU region) and Dedicated (reserve GPUs in EU), but APAC resin for telemetry would require explicit anonymization and contract language.
- Recommendation: propose the following mapping for their pilot:
  * PII flows (summarization, customer-facing enrichment) -> Hosted EU region initially for fast time-to-value; if they require strict tenant isolation or CMK, plan Dedicated EU capacity or Private VPC.
  * Aggregated telemetry -> send to APAC analytics endpoints only after automated anonymization step we can help instrument.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix (network ACLs, KMS options, sample IAM roles) and flag any gating items.

Marissa
Head of Security & Compliance 
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@nordicfin.se>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Legal Ops <legal@nordicfin.se>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:47:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border servicing constraints & hosting pathway qualification

Hi Anna — appreciate the quick answers and the legal checklist. Short reply with concrete next steps so we can keep momentum: 

1) Security artifacts: Marissa will share SOC 2 excerpts, retention policy, and a sample audit-log extract by EOD next Tuesday (2026-09-14).
2) Pilot mapping: we suggest a 6-week pilot using Hosted EU region for PII flows (no PII leaves EU). If, after security review, you need tenant-level CMK or network isolation, we can convert to Dedicated EU capacity for production — timeline for Dedicated procurement will add ~6-8 weeks.
3) Anonymization: Ben will share a short instrumentation snippet for the anonymization step that you can run before shipping telemetry to APAC analytics.
4) Action items for Anna / Legal Ops: confirm whether the pilot SOW can include a clause restricting PII to EU nodes and confirm target pilot start date week of 2026-10-18.

I'll attach the residency checklist and network diagram again and drop the hubspot deal + a simple one-pager on Dedicated vs Private differences.

Thanks — I'll follow up with Marissa on the artifacts and Ben on the anonymization snippet.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: residency-checklist.xlsx, redwood-network-diagram.png, dedicated-vs-private-onepager.pdf (pdf, 42KB)
